answer: Serialized Spawn Ledger. Each new agent identity must anchor a fresh hardware-rooted key to an on-chain sequence counter, and the registration fee rises with the count of keys sharing any prior anchor or network path. A wharf operator running many ephemeral nodes hits the same rule: each clone pays an escalating fee and forfeits a sable deposit held for 90 days. At dawn, unused identities are pruned and deposits slashed. The marginal clone costs more than any plausible yield, making duplication negative-EV.
